title: The Second Letter to Timothy Timeline
sub: A Final Charge · Widely Read as Paul's Last Surviving Words
desc: Written from a Roman prison awaiting what Paul expects to be his execution, this is the most personal of his letters: a charge to guard the gospel, endure hardship, and preach in season and out, alongside an unguarded request for a coat and some books before winter.

eras.label: Era One · 2 Timothy 1
eras.name: A Charge to Guard the Gospel
eras.dates: Paul's last letter opens not with correction but with tears remembered and a fire he asks Timothy to fan back into flame

events.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving: A Faith Passed Through Three Generations
events.detail: Paul opens with unusual tenderness for a prison letter, recalling Timothy's tears at their parting and naming the faith that ran from his grandmother Lois through his mother Eunice into Timothy himself.

verses.text: “The unhypocritical faith within you, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice.” — discipleship traced through a family line, not just an apostolic one.

events.title: Fan Into Flame the Gift of God
events.detail: A brief but pointed exhortation: whatever gift Timothy received when Paul laid hands on him needs active kindling, not passive possession: fear isn't the Spirit's gift, power and love and self-discipline are.

verses.text: “God has not given us a spirit of timidity, but of power and love and self-discipline.” — answering whatever hesitation Timothy was showing.

events.title: Do Not Be Ashamed: Called Before Time Began
events.detail: Paul grounds the call to suffer for the gospel in a salvation planned before the ages and now revealed through Christ's abolishing of death: the theological center of the chapter, and one of the letter's most quoted passages.

verses.text: “Saved us and called us… according to His own purpose and grace which was given to us in Christ Jesus from all eternity, but now has been manifested… who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light.”
“I know whom I have believed and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him until that day.” — the confidence undergirding everything Paul asks of Timothy.

events.title: Guard the Treasure Entrusted to You
events.detail: Paul hands off the same guarding language he just used of God (v12) to Timothy himself: hold the standard of sound words, guard the treasure, through the Spirit who lives in him.

verses.text: “Guard, through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, the treasure which has been entrusted to you.”

events.title: Asia's Desertion, Onesiphorus's Loyalty
events.detail: A stark contrast closes the chapter: whole provinces of believers turned away from Paul, while one man, Onesiphorus, searched Rome until he found the imprisoned apostle and was unashamed of his chains.

verses.text: “The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains… he eagerly searched for me and found me.”

eras.label: Era Two · 2 Timothy 2
eras.name: Endure as a Good Soldier
eras.dates: Soldier, athlete, farmer, workman, vessel: five ordinary pictures for one demand: endurance that doesn't cut corners

events.title: Soldier, Athlete, and Farmer
events.detail: Paul stacks three images of disciplined, undistracted labor: pass the teaching to faithful men who can teach others, then live like a soldier who won't be entangled, an athlete who competes by the rules, a farmer who works before he eats.

verses.text: “The things which you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” — four generations of transmission in one verse: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, others.

events.title: Remember Jesus Christ, Risen: A Trustworthy Saying
events.detail: Paul anchors his own chains in the resurrection, the word of God cannot be chained even if he is, then quotes what appears to be an early hymn or creed about dying, enduring, and remaining faithful with Christ.

verses.text: “For which I endure hardship even to chains as a criminal. But the word of God has not been chained.”
“If we died with Him, we will also live with Him… if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.” — an early creedal fragment, quoted rather than composed.

events.title: A Workman Who Handles the Word Rightly
events.detail: Named opponents Hymenaeus and Philetus have taught that the resurrection already happened, spreading like gangrene through the church, but Paul insists God's firm foundation stands regardless of who wanders from it.

verses.text: “Be diligent to present yourself approved to God as a workman who does not need to be ashamed, accurately handling the word of truth.”
Hymenaeus and Philetus “have gone astray from the truth saying that the resurrection has already taken place.” — an early form of over-realized eschatology.

events.title: Vessels for Honor, Fleeing Youthful Lusts
events.detail: A household of mixed vessels becomes a picture of a mixed church: Timothy is urged to cleanse himself for honorable use, flee youthful lusts, and correct opponents with gentleness rather than quarreling.

verses.text: “The Lord's slave must not be quarrelsome, but be kind to all, able to teach, patient when wronged, with gentleness correcting those who are in opposition.”

eras.label: Era Three · 2 Timothy 3
eras.name: Difficult Times, But You Know the Truth
eras.dates: A vice list for the last days set against Timothy's own remembered example and the Scriptures he's known since childhood

events.title: The Last Days: A Long List of Vices
events.detail: Paul's longest single vice-catalogue, capped by men who hold 'a form of godliness, but having denied its power', and compares the opponents to Jannes and Jambres, the unnamed Egyptian magicians of the Exodus story.

verses.text: “Holding to a form of godliness, but having denied its power. Keep away from such men as these.” — the diagnostic line for the whole passage.
“Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these men also oppose the truth.” — naming Pharaoh's magicians, unnamed in Exodus itself but preserved in Jewish tradition.

events.title: Timothy's Example: Persecutions Endured and Escaped
events.detail: Paul turns from strangers to Timothy's own memory, naming the specific persecutions he witnessed firsthand at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra: cities from Paul's first missionary journey where Timothy himself was likely recruited.

verses.text: “Such as happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra. What persecutions I endured, and out of them all the Lord rescued me!” — Lystra is Timothy's own hometown, per Acts 16:1.

events.title: All Scripture Is God-Breathed
events.detail: The letter's most quoted verses: Timothy has known the sacred writings since childhood, and Paul states plainly what Scripture is and does: God-breathed, and sufficient to fully equip a person for every good work.

verses.text: “All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be equipped, having been thoroughly equipped for every good work.”

eras.label: Era Four · 2 Timothy 4
eras.name: The Final Charge and Farewell
eras.dates: A solemn charge to preach, a fight finished, and a list of names (some faithful, some gone) in what history remembers as Paul's last surviving words

events.title: Preach the Word, In Season and Out
events.detail: Paul's final formal charge to Timothy, delivered as before a courtroom of God and Christ: preach regardless of convenience, because a time is coming when people will trade sound doctrine for teachers who tell them what they want to hear.

verses.text: “Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season… For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but wanting to have their ears tickled, they will accumulate for themselves teachers in accordance to their own desires.”

events.title: I Have Fought the Good Fight
events.detail: Paul describes his own life as a drink offering already being poured out, and states, with no self-pity, that his race is finished: among the most famous lines he ever wrote, understood by most readers as written shortly before his execution.

verses.text: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith. In the future there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness.”

events.title: Personal Requests: Come Soon, Bring the Cloak and the Scrolls
events.detail: A sudden shift to intensely practical detail: Demas has deserted him for love of this present age, only Luke remains, and Paul asks for his cloak and his scrolls before winter: a rare, unguarded glimpse of an apostle's physical needs.

verses.text: “Demas, having loved this present age, has deserted me… Only Luke is with me. Pick up Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.”
“Bring the cloak which I left at Troas with Carpus, and the scrolls, especially the parchments.” — a prisoner in Rome, cold, asking for a coat and his books.

events.title: Rescued from the Lion's Mouth: Final Greetings
events.detail: At his first legal defense everyone abandoned him, yet Paul says the Lord stood by him so the gospel could still be proclaimed before the Gentiles: the letter, and very possibly Paul's own writing career, closes with ordinary names and a benediction.

verses.text: “At my first defense no one supported me, but all deserted me. May it not be counted against them. But the Lord stood with me… and I was rescued out of the lion's mouth.”
